items.title: Honkai: Star Rail's Yao Guang Gets a New 1/8 Scale Figure in the Gift+ Series
items.summary: ADK Emotions is now taking pre-orders for Yao Guang, the newest addition to Myethos
items.content:
ADK Emotions Co., Ltd. is now taking pre-orders for a new product from Myethos: Yao Guang, the latest addition to the Gift+ series from the game Honkai: Star Rail.

Myethos Japan online store product page — purchase here:

"Nice to meet you. I'm General Yao Guang, Seer Strategist of the Xianzhou Yuque. Feel free to just call me by my name."

Yao Guang, the new addition to the Gift+ series from the wildly popular game Honkai: Star Rail, now comes to life as a 1/8 scale figure!

Yao Guang stands with elegant poise, her expression carrying its usual calm smile.

Her long dress, rendered in a beautiful gradient, looks as though it were woven from flowing light. The hem spreads lightly outward, evoking a peacock spreading its feathers, while pearl-toned accents scattered throughout catch the light like a shimmering, flowing galaxy.

Ornaments adorning her shoulders and tassels hanging from her ears highlight her graceful beauty, while the intricate silver detailing covering the figure creates an elegant, refined atmosphere reminiscent of classical antiquity.

Even faced with a solemn, unfathomable destiny, Yao Guang's smile never wavers. A quiet flame burns in her bright eyes, and having seen through countless threads of cause and effect, she fearlessly steps forward into the whirlpool of fate.

Trailblazer — won't you walk alongside Yao Guang and rewrite the galaxy's fate?

Specifications: Includes dedicated stand; overall height: approx. 214mm; PVC & ABS & metal

September 16, 2026, 9:00 PM to November 30, 2026, 11:59 PM

The photos shown are of a sample still in development. The actual product may differ in some specifications.

items.title: The Aeon Aha Will be Playable in Honkai: Star Rail 4.7
items.summary: A 4.7 five-star in Honkai: Star Rail will make Aha the first playable Aeon class character in the game when she debuts later in 2026.
items.content:
We’ll be getting what might be our first playable Aeon in Honkai: Star Rail with the debut of Aha in 4.7. HoYoVerse teased the new unit on social media with official character art and first details about her path. She’ll be a featured five-star when she shows up.

Prior to the appearance of the playable version of Aha, we actually saw her show up in the game’s story. During the Planarcadia storyline, the Trailblazer and allies encountered her as an NPC. For this version of her, she will feature an entirely different look that features the same sort of color scheme as Sparxie, rather than her previous original design. There’s no reference to the part she played when she showed up as an NPC in past quests.

As predicted from the Elation Aeon, she’ll walk that path. It’s not sure how that will work, given it relies on building up Punchline and Aha Instant additional attacks. She’ll deal Quantum damage whenever she strikes foes.

Here’s her full art for the upcoming character. That highlights her new dress and official color scheme, with reference to the Aha Instant behind her.

It’s unknown when we might see her. We know Honkai: Star Rail 4.6 will debut on September 29, 2026. That’s because the Aventurine alt banner ends on September 28, 2026. The one confirmed unit for that next patch so far is the IPC unit Pearl .

Honkai: Star Rail is available on the PS5, PC, and mobile devices and will get the playable Aeon Aha in its 4.7 update.

items.title: Shanghai Opens First Criminal Case Against Video Game Leaks
items.summary: One suspect told investigators he thought deleting the videos after warnings would avoid consequences.
items.content:
Shanghai police have launched the city’s first criminal case against video game content leaks, arresting three suspects accused of posting unreleased material from popular games online.

The leak, reported by domestic media on Friday, involves videos showing upcoming scenes and characters from games developed by miHoYo, including “Genshin Impact” and “Honkai: Star Rail,” two globally popular online games with millions of players worldwide. The leaked material was posted on Chinese streaming site BiliBili, private online groups, and a gaming wiki.

In China, gaming leaks have traditionally been handled through platform takedowns and account bans rather than criminal prosecution. The investigation signals a tougher approach to unauthorized distribution of game content.

MiHoYo first reported the case to local authorities in October. Though the videos were taken down within days, they drew more than 100,000 views each, with total views exceeding 13 million.

Police said the three suspects — all in their 20s — posted the content to attract traffic and earn in-game rewards. One suspect surnamed Zhou, identified as the original source of the leaks, has been detained. The other two, accused of reposting the videos, have been transferred to prosecutors on charges of copyright infringement.

Zhou holds a doctoral degree in mathematics and is well known in gaming communities for his technical expertise. In February, miHoYo filed a lawsuit in the U.S. state of Georgia seeking to shut down the private wiki Zhou allegedly operated, which provided “Genshin Impact” tutorials and character guides.

“We just did this for fun,” Zhou told investigators. “We thought we would be fine as long as we deleted the videos after receiving warnings from the platforms.”

In recent years, an increasing number of developers have turned to legal action to curb leaks. In 2024, a court in Chengdu, capital of China’s southwestern Sichuan province, sentenced a man to three years in prison and fined him 300,000 yuan ($43,600) for leaking future character skins from gaming giant Tencent’s “Honor of Kings.”

Last April, the Supreme People’s Court issued guidelines clarifying how criminal law applies to IP violations, including copyright infringement. Shanghai has also since launched collaborative IP protection mechanisms for its online game industry.

Luo Xi, legal director at miHoYo, told local media that leaks can “create operational challenges for game developers, affecting release plans and overall product management.”

items.title: Why Honkai: Star Rail players talk quitting the game
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail players and creators are debating whether to quit amid complaints about power creep, endgame design, events and story presentation.
items.content:
A wave of Reddit posts and YouTube videos about quitting Hoyoverse ‘s Honkai: Star Rail has put long-running complaints over power creep, endgame design and story presentation back at the centre of the game’s community debate.

The discussion does not establish that Star Rail is facing a measurable player exodus. The sources reviewed offer no player-count data. What they do show is a recurring concern from active and former players: the game can demand continued investment while giving some of them fewer reasons to log in.

YouTuber Pixel Tree , who said he had not played Star Rail for some time, argued that the current criticism was more notable because it was coming from the game’s own community rather than rival fandoms. He said seeing regular Star Rail creators express frustration suggested there was a genuine issue behind the wider social media debate.

Power creep is one of the complaints that appears most consistently across the Reddit post and creator videos. Players argue that the gap between older and newer characters has grown enough to change how they approach pulling, building and spending on units.

Read more: Hoyoverse announces Genshin Impact 7.1 Special Program date

GachaNekoVT , who said he still plays Star Rail, argued that the problem goes beyond new characters simply being stronger. Players may begin wondering how long a newly acquired character will remain useful before another unit performs the same role more effectively.

That can also make spending harder to justify. Building a character can take weeks or months, while obtaining higher Eidolons or signature Light Cones can require further investment. The concern is that the value of that investment may decline much faster than players expect.

Similar complaints in the material point to newer characters replacing older ones with comparable but stronger kits, widening the perceived gap between generations of units.

Endgame design has intensified that frustration. Players criticised rising enemy health and mechanics that favour particular character archetypes or team compositions. The Reddit author described the meta as increasingly punishing for players who want to continue using older characters.

Read more: Genshin Impact 7.0: Are Flins and Ineffa worth pulling?

Kekvin agreed that recent bosses and endgame modes can restrict viable teams, although he noted that power creep itself is hardly new to Star Rail. His criticism focused more on how newer encounters can turn difficulty into a question of which characters a player owns rather than how they use them.

The Reddit post from DependentNo1079 described Planarcadia as a story that was not necessarily bad but had failed to meet expectations. Its author pointed to repetitive animations, lengthy dialogue and presentation that can struggle to make major story moments feel distinct.

Pixel Tree discussed similar complaints, including repeated character poses, reused models and limited animation. The material also highlights the game’s frequent reliance on text screens during story sequences, an approach that has become a recurring joke within the community.

GachaNekoVT raised a different problem with the writing itself. He praised Star Rail’s characters and music but argued that recent stories can become difficult to follow because of the volume of lore, terminology and exposition.

items.title: Honkai: Nexus Anima is a fun creature collector with an incomprehensible story
items.summary: Honkai: Nexus Anima spins off with creature collecting auto-battling gameplay, making for a fun change of pace, though it doesn't quite fit the story.
items.content:
It’s a big deal whenever HoYoverse launches a new game. While it’s true that a new gacha game pops up almost every day, those same gacha games are almost all lifting references or mechanics wholesale from HoYoverse titles. Genshin Impact put the company on the map and shaped what modern gacha games are, and they’ve followed up that hit with Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero, each one making waves and shaking up the industry just a little bit more. It’s safe to assume that HoYoverse wants that same kind of impact from their next major title, and Honkai: Nexus Anima is certainly shaping up to be a swing in a wild new direction. Unfortunately, it’s a big swing that doesn’t fully connect at this time.

Honkai: Nexus Anima is a pretty unique mix of genres and gameplay hooks. While it’s built around creature collecting and will naturally draw comparisons to Pokémon, you aren’t then taking these monsters into turn-based 1v1 battles. Instead, you use them to dive into Teamfight Tactics-style auto battles between big teams of Anima – the creature name in this world.

I’ve always been curious about these sort of idle-battler games, but never met one that hooked me. Using that formula within the context of an anime gacha game, plus mixing in tons of cute collectable creatures, totally does it for me. At first, the depth of combat doesn’t feel particularly vast. There certainly isn’t a high skill ceiling to this style of battle, even as you start mixing in numerous abilities from your Eidos companions. It’s still satisfying to play, but there is a lack of mechanical difficulty at this stage which would need to ramp up to make for a truly satisfying and absorbing endgame.

Outside of battles, Honkai: Nexus Anima will be pretty familiar to you if you’ve dabbled in HoYoverse games. The tutorial section has you exploring some small interactive maps as your chosen protagonist, feeling pretty similar to the small zones of Zenless Zone Zero or Honkai: Star Rail. When you get into the meat of the game, though, you’re tossed into a pretty rich and wide map that combines the scale of a Genshin Impact region with modern buildings and whimsical fantasy meadows.

The game is beautiful, the map is beautiful, the characters you meet are beautiful…but I don’t quite know how to describe them. There isn’t a very clear genre or style to attach Honkai: Nexus Anima to – the other games in the Honkai line were always melting pots of influence that lean heavily toward sci-fi, and Genshin Impact feels similar with a further lean towards Japanese high-fantasy. Honkai: Nexus Anime is bright and bubbly, but impossible to place in the same way.

The story, meanwhile, is not bright or bubbly, but it’s certainly equally incomprehensible. HoYoverse games have an habit of repeating the same two-hit combo in their stories of giving you an amnesiac protagonist, and tossing you into a multidimensional, intergalactic story full of multiple tiers of entities and shadowy realms and world-ending threats and confusing proper nouns. Honkai: Nexus Anima lays it on as thick as usual, with all the gravitas of a grim sci-fi epic. This is a cutesy creature collector, though. The music is whimsical, and the menus are bubbly, but there’s a disconnect between the vibe the game seems to be cultivating and the vibe the story itself is doing. The dense multi-dimensional gacha stories are an acquired taste to start with, but it’s especially egregious here, and I didn’t feel an investment in or understanding of the world I’m exploring because of it.

And that’s a shame, because it really is so much fun to explore this world. Each Anima you bond with can be summoned outside of battles to wander around with you and bust out their unique abilities. One type can smash through walls, while another can become a hilarious improvised trampoline for you to bounce off. I was pretty addicted to the gameplay loop I found myself in, where I’d spend time exploring the world to find new Anima, then I’d dive into battles to see which ones fit together best in a team. And then, once I found a team I liked, I could set out to keep training and uncapping my favourite Anima to make them as strong as possible.

It’s so much fun to play Honkai: Nexus Anima and it’s take on the creature collecting genre, but from the closed beta test, that gets lost in the bland world and incomprehensible story. Being invested in the characters and the story is my biggest reason for picking up a gacha game, and without that, I already have one foot out the door with Honkai: Nexus Anima. I’m hopeful that, as we head towards the full release, HoYoverse can massage these problems and reel me back in.

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail 4.3 guide: Events, free Jades, & banner schedule
Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 The Lethe Below the Living Officially Revealed
items.summary: Version 4.3 smooths some stuff out on 'The Lethe Below the Living' next month.
items.content:
SINGAPORE, May 22, 2026 — Global interactive entertainment brand HoYoverse announced today that the brand-new Version 4.3 of Honkai: Star Rail, The Lethe Below the Living, will launch on June 1, 2026. This version will continue the story of Planarcadia. The Trailblazer and Mortenax Blade will separately venture into the World in Canvas and, under the dual oppression of Lord Ravager Asat Pramad's shadow and the seal of the Aeon Voracity, confront the finale of Blade's age-old fate. Click to watch the Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 Trailer: https://youtu.be/lW5ndcGuw2c Click here to get the media kit: https://hoyoverse.box.com/s/hdtkl6ult62s40ggi964sd4n2ahpzgf3 The secret sealed deep within Planarcadia will reach its official revelation in this version. At the end of the picturesque realm lies the divine husk of the Aeon, the Voracity. This ancient entity, presiding over desire and devouring, is the very crux of Blade's wager on this journey. Bearing the flesh of Shuhu from within two hundred thousand Joy Ascendants, Blade has chosen to step onto the board himself. He seeks to borrow the power of the Voracity to melt away the Shuhu within his own body, bringing a final end to this long-enduring curse. However, whether this action ultimately leads to death or rebirth remains a blank in Elio's script, and the answer will be witnessed firsthand by the Trailblazer. Meanwhile, the Trailblazer will also depart for Inkford Hermitage, the boundary between this life and the World in Canvas, to transmit a warning regarding the threat of Asat Pramad to Graphia, who is stationed there. This ancestor of the Murata family, known as the "Mother of Imagenesis," has lived in this world for a full millennium. As early as Amber Era 2148, she used a single brush to encanvas the entirety of Ahatopia, fending off the invasion of the Demons From Beyond, but at the cost of burdening every subsequent generation of the Murata family with the "Weathering Curse." With the official debut of this millennial figure who has witnessed many major events in the cosmos, she may offer new answers regarding the Graphia family, Phantasmoon Games, and even the numerous mysteries surrounding Himeko. In this update, Mortenax Blade, a 5-star Fire-Type character following the Path of Nihility, officially makes his debut. This swordsman, once stricken with mara, leading him to join the Stellaron Hunters and await his "death in the script" across the long years, will face a major turning point in his destiny in this version. In combat, Mortenax Blade can use his Ultimate, "Fornax Ex Corpore" to deploy a special Bounded Field and enter an enhanced state. While the Bounded Field is active, all enemies receive increased DMG. Upon entering this enhanced state, Mortenax Blade unlocks his Skill, utilizing a Sword Formation to deal even more DMG to enemies while gaining a brand-new, more powerful Ultimate. Furthermore, every time an ally attacks an enemy, they inflict a debuff on the target and accumulate a special Charge for Mortenax Blade. Once this Charge is full, he automatically uses his Skill once and regenerates extra Energy. Alongside this version update, the "Gift of Tempered Blade" event will also kick off: After obtaining Mortenax Blade from Warping, players can claim a brand-new Trailblaze Outfit piece, "Karmic Fire of the Distant Shore," for free. Meanwhile, Yao Guang will have a rerun during the first-half Warps, while the second half will feature the limited return of Cyrene and Phainon. As for version events, the IPC is launching the "Wispae Amusement Park" within the World in Canvas. Taking on the role of "Chief Planner," the Trailblazer will map out visitor routes and place amusement rides across different themed zones to attract wispae to come and play. At the same time, a new "Starward Mode" will be added to three challenge gameplay modes: Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. In this mode, the Trailblazer will need to set up 3 teams to take on 3 different stages. Clearing each gameplay with full stars will reward an extra 100 Stellar Jades per phase, amounting to an additional 300 Stellar Jades in total across all three modes. Furthermore, Honkai: Star Rail has officially announced its collaboration with UGREEN. Collaboration merchandise and various online and offline events will gradually roll out across multiple countries and regions, with more details to be revealed at a later date. Finally, this summer, the Holy Grail War will ignite once again. Stay tuned for more details! Honkai: Star Rail is now available on PC, iOS, Android, Epic Games Store, and PS5, and has exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms. In 2023, the game won Apple's App Store iPhone Game of the Year, Google Play's Best Game, and BEST MOBILE GAME by The Game Awards. In 2024, it received the Golden Joystick Awards Still Playing Award (Mobile) and PlayStation® Partner Awards 2024 PARTNER AWARD among other honors. The game has been rated Teen by the ESRB and is also classified as PEGI 12. If you wish to learn more details, please visit https://hsr.hoyoverse.com or follow @HonkaiStarRail on Twitter (X), Instagram, and Facebook. About Honkai: Star Rail Honkai: Star Rail is a space fantasy RPG title with a journey through immense worlds of the unknown. The player takes on the role of "Trailblazer," a courageous individual implanted with a powerful artifact, Stellaron, and bearing the determination to unravel the mysteries surrounding the fabled "Cancer of All Worlds" and Aeons. The game features fantasy elements with myths and legends integrated into the space sci-fi story. Combined with the intuitive turn-based combat system, diverse and distinctive companions, and immersive storylines that together compose an interstellar melody filled with captivating worlds, each brimming with unique cultures, awe-inspiring landscapes, and mythical wonders to explore. About HoYoverse HoYoverse is committed to providing immersive virtual world experiences to players around the world. We have brought fans popular games including Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, Honkai Impact 3rd, Tears of Themis, and Zenless Zone Zero, as well as a wide range of entertainment content. Community is at the heart of everything we do. We are devoted to engaging fans and fostering an enthusiastic and inclusive global community that provides access and encouragement for people to share their passion for ACG (Animation, Comics, and Games) through their own creativity and skills. Pushing the boundaries of imagination, we consistently explore cutting-edge game development technologies, and have accumulated leading technical capabilities in cel shading, cloud gaming, and other fields. In the future, we will continue to expand our content production, technology research, and publishing duties through operations in offices in Singapore, Montreal, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Seoul, and other areas. items.title: Giving a game another chance
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it. That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I...
items.content:
Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it.

That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I had to stop playing because of bugs. I also stopped because it was really laggy, but I realized when I started playing again this past December that I had actually originally played on the European server rather than the American one, which was why it was lagging.

Now that I’ve started playing it again for the last four months, I’m wishing I’d never quit.

The game’s story is amazing. With games like HSR where the main character is a self-insert, I tend to fully lean into that role. As such, whenever a major twist happens to a character that the main character has bonded with, I really feel it due to the immersion.

Another thing I like about the story is that HSR keeps you on your toes because it isn’t afraid to kill off playable characters.

I’d played a different game from HoYoverse before HSR, and it wouldn’t dream of killing a playable character, so I went into HSR thinking it’d be the same. That idea went out the window on my second day of playing with the first of many playable character deaths.

Because of that, you end up wanting to make sure you own your favorite characters in case you never see them in the game again. However, since HSR is a gacha game, you’re not guaranteed to get the characters you want when they’re available without spending money.

At least that’s what you’d think, but from my experience, HSR is the easiest gacha game I’ve played when it comes to getting the characters you want without spending money.

I’ve managed to get three characters I’ve wanted along with two of their exclusive items without spending money. That’s because HSR makes it really easy to get the in-game currency for pulling characters. That means if you just want to get a character for the sake of having them, you can.

In fact, I’d say HSR is probably the only gacha game where you don’t have to spend real money. I only spent money on cosmetics, but most cosmetics are free rewards from permanent events.

The only negative thing I have to say about the game is that the newer main quests are fairly long.

The latest finished questline takes 62 hours to complete, and the entire main quest line is currently over 100 hours. Because of that, if you have a busy daily schedule, it could take a while to complete. It is possible to finish in a week, but based on personal experience, I wouldn’t recommend it.

The length aside, I would highly recommend this game, especially since it’s free on PC and you don’t even need a gaming one as I play on my laptop. With the three years of content in the game so far, I can’t wait to see where it goes from here.

items.title: MAPPA, HoYoverse Release 'Animation Concept Trailer' for Honkai: Star Rail Game (Updated)
items.content:
HoYoverse revealed during a livestream for its Honkai: Star Rail game on Friday that it and MAPPA have co-produced an "animation concept trailer" for the game. The trailer, viewable below, is titled "Death in the Afternoon."

Yuzuru Tachikawa ( Mob Psycho 100 , Death Parade director) directed the trailer and Kayoko Ishikawa ( Sarazanmai , ZENSHU. ) was the character designer. The end of the above video features the words " MAPPA Honkai: Star Rail Animation A New Story Awaits."

The HoYoverse staff had introduced the video in the livestream as a "mysterious collaboration project." HoYoverse's press release about the livestream announcements stated that at the end of the livestream, "...the original animation project co-produced by HoYoverse and MAPPA premiered its concept trailer, 'Death in the Afternoon.' Please look forward to the continuing cosmic adventures!"

The livestream and HoYoverse's press release did not give any further details. It is currently unclear if the "original animation project" is the above trailer, or if the collaboration will include other works.

Update: ANN reached out to HoYoverse for clarification, and the company provided the following response:

HoYoverse launched its Honkai: Star Rail game for PC and mobile in April 2023, and then for PlayStation 5 in October 2023. The game has exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms.

The game will launch its Version 4.2 patch on April 22. The patch will celebrate the game's third anniversary.

HoYoverse's earlier game Genshin Impact launched a "long-term collaboration project" with ufotable in 2022. The project is still in production.

Sources: Press release, Honkai: Star Rail game's YouTube channel ( link 2 )

items.title: Hands on with the Honkai: Star Rail v4.0 experience
items.summary: This HoyoVerse train just keeps on chugging!
items.content:
The last article I wrote for Honkai: Star Rail was going over the details of the upcoming Version 4.0 release . Since then, HoYoverse generously offered up the opportunity to play Version 4.0 and experience Planarcadia early. Having spent about a dozen hours or so playing with the new characters, experiencing the story, and generally taking in the sights and sounds of Planarcadia, I’m prepared to share my thoughts on all of it.

It’s best to start off with the main attraction of Version 4.0: Planarcadia. This new planet is a fictional world come to life and boy does it leave a fantastic first impression. Full of the kind of sights and sounds you’d expect from an Asian city brimming with life. Exploration is a blast with all the alleys and little nooks to find, the platforming segments that can either help you navigate across certain parts of the city or find chests within them. There’s also a new style of puzzles that require you to rotate a 2D plane in a 3D space to “paint” certain parts of it to make them solid and let you platform with those objects. Planarcadia is so full of whimsy and still has some of the overhang of a crime family really enabling a super unique feeling planet compared to what we’ve had with previous locations such as the Xianzhou or Amphoreus.

The two new characters following the path of Elation feel great, even if the Aha Moment is a little overstimulating sometimes. Sparxie and Yao Guang fit on a team together like a glove to demolish all the bosses I’ve thrown them against. I’m eager to see where the new path goes with time, especially since we only have the two characters currently. Even as of the live public server branch, we’re unsure when Elation Trailblazer will make their debut, so keep an eye on that as versions progress beyond 4.0. You’ll need to get a hold of new Elation Light Cones as well since they obviously can’t use the other Paths’ options. Burning skill points to increase the Elation stacks until Aha decides he’s satisfied and steps in for a big attack feels really great and it has me curious what future Elation characters might do when they trigger their own Aha Moments.

Not to mention that for new players, you’ve got the opportunity to really kickstart a team of your choice with a new planet. We’re at a point in the game where there’s so many options for characters you can pick from and build around, and 4.0 introducing Elation means that as a new player, you can jump in and get a headstart on pulling for that archetype. Especially with a new Novaflare round of buffs, there’s even more options than before bringing older characters back into the limelight. The Black Swan and Sparkle buffs are so massive that people running DoT teams or any team using an action advance support such as Bronya or Sunday have another insane option. Sparkle was always good, but her Novaflare enables her to further buff your DPS units to extreme levels. Black Swan’s Novaflare was even more insane and rocketed her back up to the top for damage even as a DoT unit. Combined with the option to pick a free character including units like Sparkle, Kafka (who works great in DoT teams), and more, you really can’t go wrong in Planarcadia and the Version 4.0 patch from what I’ve gotten to experience.

Between the free characters, the great change of pace in the story from the latter half of Amphoreus (if you’ve played it, you know), the new cityscape that is quite honestly my new favorite location in the game, and all the new characters to look forward to, you really should make a return to Star Rail if you’ve been away for a minute and are curious about where we’re at. If you’re new, definitely consider giving it a shot. There’s even a bonus to let you convert trace materials for leveling character skills at a 1 to 1 ratio this time instead of a 2 for 1, so you really can kickstart your Elation team. With characters being important again like Silver Wolf, Blade, and Himeko, as well as new faces like Sparxie, Yao Guang, Ashveil, and Pearl, I think 4.0 is just the start of a real treat of a patch cycle for Honkai: Star Rail.
